source_refs.note: Exercise 10.1, Question 8: book page 278 (Q1-Q24). The book prints no answers for Exercise 10.1.

blocks.explanation:
Yahan do alag ratios hain, \(\cot\) aur \(\csc\). Do ratios ke saath kaam mushkil hai, is liye identity \(\csc^{2}x = 1 + \cot^{2}x\) se sab kuch \(\cot x\) mein le aayenge.
Find kya karna hai? Principal solutions aur general solution.
Phir \(\cot^{2}x = \frac{1}{3}\) se \(\tan x = \pm\sqrt{3}\) banega, jo Question 6 wali hi equation hai.
Plan: identity, \(\tan\) mein badlo, dono cases, period \(\pi\), aur defined hone ka check.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(3\cot^{2}x + 3\csc^{2}x = 5\).
Maloom karna: principal solutions aur general solution.
Tareeqa: \(\csc^{2}x = 1 + \cot^{2}x\) se equation ko ek hi ratio mein laayenge, phir \(\tan x\) ke liye hal karenge.

\(\csc^{2}x\) ki jagah rakhein
\[3\cot^{2}x + 3(1 + \cot^{2}x) = 5\]
\[6\cot^{2}x + 3 = 5\]
\[\cot^{2}x = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: Pythagorean identity \(1 + \cot^{2}x = \csc^{2}x\). Bracket kholne par \(3\cot^{2}x + 3\cot^{2}x = 6\cot^{2}x\), phir 3 ko doosri taraf le ja kar 6 se divide kiya.

Tangent mein badlein
\[\tan^{2}x = 3\]
\[\tan x = \pm\sqrt{3}\]
Kyun: \(\tan x = \frac{1}{\cot x}\), to \(\tan^{2}x\) bhi \(\frac{1}{3}\) ka ulta, yani 3. Tangent ki values humein zyada achhi tarah yaad hain. Square root ke saath \(\pm\).

Hal karein (reference angle \(\frac{\pi}{3}\))
\[\tan x = \sqrt{3}:\ x = \dfrac{\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{4\pi}{3}\]
\[\tan x = -\sqrt{3}:\ x = \dfrac{2\pi}{3},\ \dfrac{5\pi}{3}\]
Kyun: tangent positive ho to quadrant I aur III, negative ho to II aur IV; bilkul Question 6 ki tarah.

Kya \(\cot x\) aur \(\csc x\) defined hain?
In chaaron angles par \(\sin x \ne 0\), is liye chaaron jawab theek hain.
Kyun: \(\cot x = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\) aur \(\csc x = \frac{1}{\sin x}\) dono ke denominator mein \(\sin x\) hai; \(\sin x = 0\) wale angles (\(0, \pi, 2\pi\)) jawab ho hi nahin sakte.

General solution
Tangent ka period \(\pi\) hai:
\[\left\{\dfrac{\pi}{3} + n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{2\pi}{3} + n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Kyun: \(\frac{4\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{3} + \pi\) aur \(\frac{5\pi}{3} = \frac{2\pi}{3} + \pi\), is liye do families kaafi hain.

Tasdeeq
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}:\ 3\cdot\dfrac{1}{3} + 3\cdot\dfrac{4}{3} = 1 + 4 = 5\]
Kyun: \(\cot\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) aur \(\csc\frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\), un ke squares \(\frac{1}{3}\) aur \(\frac{4}{3}\). Baqi teen angles par bhi squares yahi hain, kyunke sirf sign badalta hai.
blocks.final_answer: Principal solutions \([0, 2\pi]\) mein: \(x = \frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{2\pi}{3}, \frac{4\pi}{3}, \frac{5\pi}{3}\). General solution: \(\left\{\frac{\pi}{3} + n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{2\pi}{3} + n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kitab mein Exercise 10.1 ke jawab chhape hue nahin hain. Is page ka har jawab hamara apna hai: qadam ba qadam hal kiya gaya, computer algebra system (sympy) se alag se check kiya gaya, aur ek solution book se bhi milaya gaya. Kitab ke examples ki tarah hum principal solutions \([0, 2\pi]\) mein aur general solution sets ke union ki shakal mein dete hain. Aap apna kaam yahan wale hal se mila kar dekh sakte hain.
